front.title: Enterprise Deployment Considerations for Standalone Merkle Tree Certificates

author.organization: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan

abstract.t: The migration of public Web PKI authentication to post-quantum mechanisms must fit enterprise certificate management and TLS termination architectures. This document examines whether an urgent need for post-quantum authentication would justify transitional support for standalone ML-DSA certificates in browser root-store policy while standalone MTC deployment capabilities mature. The scope is limited to enterprise public websites accessed by unmanaged clients using the public Web PKI. Note: a large enterprise may operate many such sites. The document describes enterprise-managed, third-party-hosted, and CDN-fronted deployments, identifies the components needed to serve standalone Merkle Tree Certificates (MTCs), and examines realistic authentication attack paths and migration priorities. It distinguishes the browser-to-edge connection from origin and internal connections, and server authentication from identity-provider login. The document draws on initial browser and TLS client testing of Trust Anchor ID signaling, and proposes interoperability tests and deployment requirements rather than changes to the MTC wire format. Relative priorities are illustrative and not empirical attack probabilities.
